# Mary

## Overview

- **Status:** alive (since v5)  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044), [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P76](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0076)</sub>  
  _previously: deceased (v2–v4)_  <sub>[v2 I An Irate Neighbor P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029), [v2 X Davy in Search of a Sensation P61](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0061)</sub>

## Appearance

Mary has a plump face featuring rosy cheeks and shining white eyes. Her hair is styled in an elaborately crimped fashion.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005)_

## Personality

Mary is a smart, vivacious, and hard-working individual who is fond of [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). While described as clean and respectful, she is also known to be sensitive, quick-tempered, gossipy, and brutally frank, often prone to being in a lecturing mood. Her speech is notably slangy and unrefined, though she actively strives to be a lady now that she is in a respectable place. In addition to her talkative nature, she possesses distinct talents, earning a reputation as the best cook in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) and excelling at playing the jew's-harp.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P28](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0028), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P87](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0087), [v5 CHAPTER VI. ## History

Mary became a widow when her son [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) was a baby and suffered from chronic illness shortly thereafter. After spending two years at an asylum, she went on to live with Mrs. [Wiley](../character/wiley.md), who starves and routinely beats her, though she was able to attend school for four winters. After being found as a ragged, forlorn waif in the old [Taylor](../character/taylor.md) barn by the Meredith children, [Faith](../character/faith.md) and [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) prepare a bed for her in the garret, where [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) comforts her night cries and fears of returning to Mrs. [Wiley](../character/wiley.md). Upon learning of Mrs. Wiley's death, Mary becomes an orphan once more, but she remains with the children and upsets [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) by warning her about the perils of potential stepmothers.

## Quotes

> "Oh, I just got to thinking of things when I was here alone. I thought of having to go back to Mrs. Wiley—and of being licked for running away—and—and—and of going to hell for telling lies. It all worried me something scandalous."
>
> — Mary — [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P106](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0106)

> "I never thought of asking for anything in particular though. Nobody in this world ever bothered themselves about me so I didn’t s’pose God would. He might take more trouble for you, seeing you’re a minister’s daughter."
>
> — Mary — [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P110](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0110)

> “Well, as to this God-matter,” said Mary stubbornly, “since you and I can’t settle it, there ain’t no use in talking more about it until we’ve a chanct to find out the rights of it. I’ll do the best I can alone till then.”
>
> — Mary — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P76](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0076)

> “I only wanted to warn you,” said Mary, rather repentantly. “Of course, your father’s so absent-minded he mightn’t happen to think of getting married again. But it’s better to be prepared.”
>
> — Mary — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P84](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0084)

> "It was just awful of you. I wouldn’t have done such a thing for the world, and I weren’t brought up in a manse—weren’t brought up anywhere—just come up."
>
> — Mary — [v5 CHAPTER XI. A DREADFUL DISCOVERY P2](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0002)

## Relationships

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary--una-meredith.md)

Mary becomes a manse companion and friend to [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) after taking up residence with the family. [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) demonstrates deep empathy for Mary's plight, comforting her during late-night fears of being sent back to her former guardian and promising to pray that she can stay in [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds). However, Mary occasionally introduces tension into their bond, such as when she upsets [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) deeply by warning her about the perils of stepmothers and predicting their father will remarry.

- Friend of — manse companion and friend (since v5)  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P124](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0124), [v5 CHAPTER VIII.
